h: Shabbos Thanksgiving Celebrates Freedom From the Evil Inclination

p: we say the psalm "Give thanks," etc.;
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem" (Tehillim 92:2).
And in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, Tzav, chapter 9):
but the thanksgiving offering will not be annulled;
but thanksgiving will not be annulled," etc.
for the Torah will never change,
and they will bring communal offerings;
but offerings that come for sin,
as they said in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Tzav),
that all the offerings come for sin:
וְאַךְ עוֹלָה בָּאָה עַל הִרְהוּר הַלֵּב
and even the olah comes for thoughts of the heart.
when the leaven in the dough will be eradicated
and there will be no sin at all,
all individual offerings will be annulled,
the first of which is the todah,
for having been saved from the leaven in the dough.
and in the future, when Hashem will be One
and it will be entirely "Who is good and does good,"
then all prayers will be annulled;
only the prayer of thanksgiving will not be annulled,
that they have been freed from the matters of this world and its vanities.
And likewise at the entry of Shabbos it is written (Bereishis 1:31):
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
"And God saw all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good";
and He saw that all was very good,
עַל כָּל הֶעָבַר בּוֹ ו׳ יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
for all that passed in the six weekdays.
And the order of the psalm comes
with four who must give thanks,
following the order of the yetzer hara's enticement,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (סוּכָּה נב, ב)
along the lines of what they said (Sukkah 52b):
"At first it calls it a passerby,
and afterward it calls it a guest,
and finally it calls it the master of the house."
תָּעוּ בַמִּדְבָּר בִּישִׁימוֹן דָּרֶךְ (תְּהִלִּים קז, ד)
"They wandered in the wilderness, in a desolate way" (Tehillim 107:4):
that is, the first enticement of the yetzer hara
is to draw a person away from Torah study,
so that he go idle like a wilderness;
and shows him that he is busy
and has no time to engage in Torah;
and even at times of leisure
it confuses his thoughts and his mind,
for it shows him that he has no repose
and is not settled in his mind
And this is "they found no city to dwell in":
"dwelling" means repose and settledness of mind;
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (עָמוֹס ח, יא)
along the lines of what is said (Amos 8:11):
And through crying out to Hashem:
to go to a city to dwell in"
"for He has sated the longing soul,
and the hungry soul He has filled with good"
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר כִּי לֶקַח טוֹב וְגוֹ׳ (מִשְׁלֵי ד, ב)
as it says, 'For I have given you good instruction, etc.'" (Mishlei 4:2).
that is, that the soul yearns
and longs for words of Torah,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת יז, א)
along the lines of what they said (Berachos 17a):
"Our will is to do Your will,
הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְמַלֵּא וּמַשְׂבִּיעַ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
Hashem Yisbarach fills and sates with words of Torah.
And this follows the order of the yetzer hara
when it is called a passerby.
"Those who sat in darkness and the shadow of death,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע אוֹסֵר אוֹתָם בְּמַאֲסָר
that is, the yetzer hara binds them in prison,
from the prison of the yetzer hara.
"For they rebelled against the words of God"
that is, the depth of the words of Torah,
"My word shall distill like the dew,"
which is the wine of the Oral Torah,
which is "the wine that I have mixed";
"and they spurned the counsel of the Most High"
for all the words of Torah
are called the counsels of the Torah,
to plant in the heart the utterance
וְאָז כְּבָר נִקְרָא הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע אוֹרֵחַ
And then the yetzer hara is already called a guest;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם כֵּן מוֹעִיל צְעָקָה
and nevertheless crying out also helps:
And afterward it speaks of the third group,
for whom the yetzer hara is called master:
"Fools, because of the way of their transgression
and because of their iniquities, are afflicted";
for the yetzer hara has already succeeded
in making them stumble in acts of transgression and iniquity:
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
along the lines of what they said in Midrash Rabbah
refer to Torah and good deeds";
"and they drew near to the gates of death";
and for this too crying out helps:
"He sends His word and heals them."
For the whole enticement of the yetzer hara
הִיא שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנְסוּ הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּלִבּוֹ
is that the words of Torah not enter his heart;
כִּי הוּא לְכָל בְּשָׂרוֹ מַרְפֵּא (מִשְׁלֵי ד, כב)
"for it is healing to all his flesh" (Mishlei 4:22).
And afterward it speaks of the fourth group,
which is those who learn Torah;
and this is "those who go down to the sea in ships"
those who go down into the sea of Talmud,
along the lines of how they explained
what is written in the Gemara, "the seafarers,"
that it refers to those who toil in the sea of Talmud;
"Ho, all who are thirsty, come to the water."
And them the yetzer hara entices:
and they imagine that they ascend to the heavens;
"they go down to the depths, etc.;
they reel and stagger like a drunkard,
and all their wisdom is swallowed up";
for the words of Torah were given
but with them the words of Torah,
which are "the wine that I have mixed,"
and this is "they reel and stagger like a drunkard,
and all their wisdom is swallowed up."
and they rejoiced because they were quiet,
and He led them to their desired haven":
for the words of Torah straighten their minds
and bring them back to the good.
this corresponds to the four kelipos
correspond to the enticement of the yetzer hara
in which it is called passerby, guest, master;
and wants to unsettle their minds
And Shabbos, which is a semblance of Olam HaBa
as if all your work were done
that is, it rectifies even the past,
along the lines of what they said (in Tanchuma, Bereishis):
just as I rested on it";
for it is written, "And God saw
and behold, it was very good"
as is written, "It is good to give thanks to Hashem";
and the meal is called a thanksgiving offering,
for one eats from the King's table.

p: except for the chametz of the todah
and the two loaves of Atzeres," etc.
For regarding all the offerings it is written (Vayikra 2:11):
וְכָל לֹא תֵאָפֶה חָמֵץ חֶלְקָם (שָׁם ו, י)
and "it shall not be baked as chametz, their portion" (6:10),
for the kohanim too are forbidden
to bake the remainders as chametz;
which signifies the time of the giving of the Torah,
וְאִיתָא (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ב, פָּסוּק יִשָּׁקֵנִי)
and it is stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2, on "Let him kiss me"):
words of Torah were implanted in their hearts, etc.;
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts."
That is, through the utterance "I am"
the words of Torah were implanted
in "the heart of the wise at his right" (Koheles 10:2),
and it is the sum of all the positive mitzvos;
and through the utterance "You shall have no"
And therefore then it was permitted to offer leaven,
the nullification of the leaven in the dough.
And likewise with the loaves of the todah,
for it is stated in the Midrash
"A parable of a king whose tenant farmers
and members of his household came to honor him," etc.;
"Neither your tenant nor a member of your household,
but he came to honor you," etc.;
"they gave him a seat of honor," etc.
That is, one who offers a todah
"For those who honor Me I will honor"
as they said in the Gemara (Chullin 133a):
כֵּן נוֹתֵן לִכְסִיל כָּבוֹד (מִשְׁלֵי כו, ח)
"so is one who gives honor to a fool" (Mishlei 26:8),
and "honor" means nothing but Torah, etc.
And therefore with the thanksgiving offering
it is permitted to eat leaven.
And likewise it is expounded there in the Midrash:
one who slaughters his yetzer in confession,"
"It is good to give thanks (lehodos) to Hashem"
"But he who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy."
And likewise it is stated in the Midrash
is like the eating of a todah,
which is eaten by all Yisrael;
and they partake from the Table on High,
and it is called the meal of the King.

p: concerning the dedication of the wall of Yerushalayim (Nechemiah 12:31):
"And I appointed two great thanksgiving choirs";
that is, the wall was then sanctified
for eating kodashim kalim within it,
and therefore it was dedicated with two todos.
why was it not dedicated with ma'aser and shelamim,
But in the Gemara (Shevuos 15a) they expounded:
and what is it? The chametz," etc.
Is there then importance before Heaven?
But because the chametz is large,
equal to three kinds of matzah.
That is, even though the kohanim
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא תֵאָפֶה חָמֵץ חֶלְקָם
nevertheless "it shall not be baked as chametz, their portion,"
for they still have a connection to leaven;
and as with the redemption from Egypt,
when leaven and chametz were forbidden to them,
until they came to the receiving of the Torah at Atzeres,
when the mitzvah of the two loaves is chametz.
which does not come for any sin,
and the leaven in the dough will be nullified
it too comes as chametz, as said.
And it is stated in the holy Zohar
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא עֵקֶב, חֵלֶק ג רעג, א)
for on it they were given," etc.
even though the tablets were not given on Shabbos;
that the Torah was given on Shabbos,
the fortieth day was not Shabbos;
does not make the hundred-twentieth day fall on Shabbos.
עַל מַאֲמַר אָנֹכִי וְלֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ
refers to the utterances "I am" and "You shall have no,"
the study of Torah was implanted in their hearts,
and through the utterance "You shall have no"
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts,
as they said (in Shir HaShirim there);
and that is the sum of positive and negative commandments;
and those are the two tablets of the heart,
"And upon their heart I will write it"
that the words of Torah were engraved in their heart,
in "the heart of the wise at his right,"
